messages:
maya: quick heads-up  i've been thinking about a formal state-machine + runbook for continuous-batcher overloads. we keep improvising and it shows in incidents.
chris: +1. we need deterministic transitions (so tests/simulations can cover them). what states are you imagining?
maya: sketch: NORMAL -> PREALERT -> DEGRADED -> DRAIN -> MICROBATCH -> RECOVERING -> NORMAL. each transition has guards and a rollback path.
devon: how do we detect PREALERT vs false positives? p99 is noisy.
anika: propose a composite "stress_index" computed per-pool every 5s: 0.6*norm(queue_depth) + 0.2*norm(eviction_rate) + 0.2*norm(p99_delta). PREALERT if stress_index > 0.6 for 3 consecutive windows. PREALERT should only escalate read-only for new long sessions.
chris: i prefer two detectors: a long-window moving average for slow ramp-ups, and a short-window spike detector for sudden bursts. if either trips, tag PREALERT but include debounce.
frank: operational goals: never impact reserved lanes automatically, always make fallback per-pool reversible, and ensure idempotent host toggles.
maya: exact runbook snippet i want in the doc: what operators run and what automation can do. e.g., automation can move pool -> PREALERT, but only oncall can move to DRAIN if reserved lanes are impacted.
chris: state machine actions (examples): PREALERT = set pool.note("prealert") + start metric-sampling; DEGRADED = enable per-tenant demotion + set stage_tag; DRAIN = stop accepting new long leases; MICROBATCH = force small requests into fastpath and route large ones to slower path; RECOVERING = gradual undo with cooldown.
devon: cache concerns: when flipping to MICROBATCH we may evict KV cache and increase backend fetches. include a post-transition grace window (30-45s) where hosts avoid aggressive eviction.
anika: rollout strategy: staged by percent of hosts (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with canary metrics. abort conditions: p95 increase > 25% OR token_cost_per_req > 1.5x OR eviction_rate spike.
frank: agree. also include a host-local safety: each host keeps local_fallback_version and only applies newer versions. that avoids split-brain double-evict.
maya: example control-plane API we can implement (small and different from other threads):
```
POST /api/v1/pools/{pool}/fallback
{
  "action": "enter",           // enter|step|rollback|exit
  "state": "MICROBATCH",      // target state
  "staged_percent": 10,        // rollout chunk
  "canary_metrics": ["p95","eviction_rate"],
  "allow_reserved": false,
  "reason": "stress_index>0.7",
  "ttl_secs": 900
}
```
chris: implementation note: handlers must be idempotent. if host receives the same command twice, second is noop. also persist last_command_id on hosts.
devon: tests: add a simulation harness that runs mixed-tenancy workloads (many short reqs + few long sessions + reserved heavy tenant), injects spikes, and asserts reserved lane p99 never exceeds SLA during automated recovery.
anika: observability: emit structured events: fallback_command, fallback_stage, host_apply, host_rollback. include tags: pool, host_id, command_id, state, staged_percent, initiator.
frank: ops playbook brief: 1) detection alert -> PREALERT notification, 2) if stress persists, automation enters DEGRADED and notifies #incidents, 3) oncall reviews and may push to DRAIN/MICROBATCH. include explicit rollback steps and postmortem checklist.
maya: add cooldown: a pool cannot re-enter DEGRADED or MICROBATCH within 10 minutes of exit unless manual override.
chris: add LeaseDecision enumeration for clarity: KEEP, DEMOTE_TO_BURST, THROTTLE, FORCE_EVICT. make decision functions deterministic and pure where possible.
devon: i'll own the simulation harness and the synthetic tenant profiles. i'll add config for short-heavy, long-context, and reserved-traffics.
anika: i'll hook up the logging schema and build a basic dashboard with the canary charts.
frank: i'll draft the operator-facing runbook and validate the control-plane auth & idempotency behavior.
maya: ops-bot: please create incident template fallback-runbook with id FR-1789556789.
ops-bot: created incident template fallback-runbook (id: FR-1789556789).
chris: i'll pick up the state-machine PR and add unit tests for transition guards + rollback. assigning to self.
maya: thanks everyone. i'll write up the RFC follow-up doc with the state graph, sample curl, and runbook link and share back here. :thumbsup:
